ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee; no refund, no account flag. Close the case.
ruling.reasoning:
The case reaches NS-1 through NS-0: the trip was cancelled by the driver who asserts the rider no-showed, so the fee stands or falls on NS-1's three elements, executed against the case record's own parameters (cancellation fee $5.00; no-show wait threshold 8 minutes, at least) [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The trace settles all three: arrival was confirmed by a driver tap at 12:17:10 [F6], the driver was 39 m from the pickup at that moment (closest approach 6 m) [F6][F1], and he then remained continuously inside the 200 m radius for 490 s until cancelling — at or above the 480 s threshold [F6], with the GPS covering the wait without a gap [F2]. The driver's physical presence is corroborated independently: stationary 41 m from the pickup from 12:16:50 to the cancellation at 12:25:20 [F3], first within 200 m at 12:15:25 with 9 min 35 s cumulative inside the radius [F2], and the platform's own record shows arrival at 12:15:25 and cancellation 9 min 55 s later [F5]. Nothing about the "at the pick-up location" requirement fails here [NS-1].

The rider's case rests on the label of the money: the record carries $5.00, not the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7], so — she argues — only NS-6's waiting fee could sustain it, and NS-6 requires boarding, a completed trip and a drop-off button tap, none of which occurred [F4][F7][NS-6]. That reading fails because NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled, rider-no-show case to NS-1, and the trace states that the case record's cancellation fee is $5.00, to be read wherever NS-1 says $6.61 [F4][F7][NS-0]. NS-6 governs an in-trip waiting fee charged after completion; it is not engaged when the trip ended in a no-show cancellation [F4][NS-6]. So the case is not a mislabelled waiting fee but an NS-1 no-show fee, and NS-1's elements are met.

The record gives no basis to suppose the driver cancelled before the window closed: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F11], the driver identified himself and the vehicle at the pickup at 12:17 [F9], warned the rider before cancelling at 12:25 "8 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10], and no GPS or timeline fact records the rider reaching the pickup point at any time before cancellation [F2][F3][F5]. The driver's written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited the full 8 minutes [F12] is a statement rather than consent evidence, but it is consistent with, and adds nothing beyond, the system records that already decide the elements [F6][F5]. Since the fee is upheld, no refund of the $5.00 arises, and the amount is nil [F7][NS-1][NS-7].

On account action: NS-2 attaches flag_account only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius — not the case here, as the tap was 39 m away [F6][NS-2]. RD-6 attaches a flag to a route-deviation case that is made out (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) plus a repeat history; this is a no-show case with no route deviation alleged, so RD-6 does not reach it [F17][RD-6]. The driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17] are profile facts and by rule cannot decide the case, and they do not attach an account action under any cited clause here [F16][F17][NS-2][RD-6]. Traffic and weather records [F13][F14][F15] and the rider's profile [F16] are not elements of any clause applied. Reviewed the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint for threats, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegations: the messages are arrival notice and cancellation notice [F9][F10][F12], and the complaint reports only timing and the charge [F4] — nothing safety-related [F1][F5].

rejected_claims.reason: Mislabels the charge: the case record's cancellation fee is $5.00 and the trace directs that figure to be read into NS-1, which the driver's cancellation satisfies on all three elements (tap at 12:17:10, 39 m away, 490 s continuous wait at or above the 480 s threshold) [F4][F6][F7][NS-0][NS-1]. NS-6 is not engaged because the trip ended in a no-show cancellation, not a completed trip with a drop-off waiting-fee tap [F4][NS-6].

The absence of a drop-off waiting-fee tap is irrelevant rather than fatal: NS-6's completion and drop-off-tap conditions apply only to an in-trip waiting fee, and this charge is assessed under NS-1 after a driver cancellation [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-6].

The record does not support 'no usable opportunity to board': the driver messaged his presence and vehicle at 12:17 [F9], stayed stationary 41 m from the pickup until 12:25:20 [F3], and no GPS or timeline fact shows the rider at the pickup before the cancellation; the rider's own arising time rests on her narrative alone, which the system records do not corroborate [F2][F5][F9][F10][F11][NS-1].

NS-2 requires an NS-1 element to fail, and none did: arrival was confirmed by the driver's tap, he was within the radius at that moment (39 m), and he waited the full recorded 8-minute threshold inside the radius before cancelling [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2]. No refund therefore falls due, so NS-7's voucher form of refund is not triggered [F7][NS-7].

NS-2 attaches a flag only where the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius, which did not happen here [F6][NS-2]; RD-6 requires an established route-deviation case (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach), and this is a no-show case with no route deviation, so the profile of 2 upheld no-show disputes cannot support an account action [F17][RD-6].

Accepted in substance but noted for the record: the driver's 'waited the full 8 minutes' reading is executed against the case record's own threshold, which the trace confirms was reached (490 s ≥ 480 s), so the fee stands under NS-1 with the $5.00 figure substituted per the trace, not under any inflated figure [F4][F6][NS-1].

Not applied: traffic band 3 and the absence of incidents concern route-deviation justification under RD-4, and no route deviation is in issue in this no-show case, so these facts neither establish nor defend the fee [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Not applied: the request that no account action follow is not an element of any clause; the panel reaches that result because NS-2's flag condition and RD-6's route-deviation branch are both unmet, and profile facts cannot decide the case either way [F16][F17][NS-2][RD-6].
